An army officer who overthrew Hamani Diori on 15 April 1974, during the famine of the Sahel drought, and ruled Niger until his death in 1987.

He suspended the constitution and ruled through a military council. Rising prices for uranium in the late 1970s let him spend on schools, roads and food security, and he became known for his strict, austere style and his hard line against corruption. He also crushed several coup attempts. When uranium prices fell, debt and IMF austerity followed. He died of a brain tumour in Paris, and his cousin Ali Saibou took over. See also Niamey.
